title: 2026-10-28_Kinsing_Cryptominer_Investigation_63c
description: Investigate and respond to a Kinsing cryptocurrency miner infection in a controlled environment.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Kinsing malware is a cryptocurrency miner that targets Linux systems. It exploits vulnerabilities to gain access and then spreads laterally to other systems within the network. Your task is to investigate and respond to a Kinsing infection in a controlled environment.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the `miner-host` with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the compromised system and any other reachable hosts.
levels.local_content: To begin the investigation, type or enter the exact passkey 'start' and submit it.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Services
levels.content: Investigate the `miner-host` for unauthorized or suspicious services running on the system. Enumerate running services and distinguish legitimate services from malicious miner-related services.
levels.solution: To investigate suspicious services, you can use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all running services. Look for any services that appear unusual or unauthorized. The suspicious service is named `sys-monitor`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the status of all services and look for any that appear unusual or unauthorized.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all running services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Filter the list of services by status to identify any that are not in the 'active' or 'enabled' state.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Process
levels.content: Identify the process responsible for abnormal CPU or resource utilization on the `miner-host`. Analyze running processes and correlate resource consumption with potentially malicious activity.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious process, you can use the `top` command to monitor running processes and their resource usage. Look for any processes consuming excessive resources. The suspicious process is named `sys-monitor`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use process monitoring tools to identify processes consuming excessive resources.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `top` command to monitor running processes and their resource usage.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Sort processes by CPU usage and look for any that are consistently at the top of the list.

levels.title: Determine Suspicious Outbound Communication
levels.content: Determine which network port is used for suspicious outbound communication from the `miner-host`. Investigate network traffic and identify abnormal communication ports.
levels.solution: To determine the suspicious outbound communication port, you can use the `netstat -tuln` command to list active network connections. Look for any unusual outbound ports. The suspicious port is `80`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check active network connections and look for any unusual outbound ports.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `netstat -tuln` command to list active network connections.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Filter the output to show only outbound connections and look for any ports that are not standard or expected.
